Refs #4189 (G5). Stacked on `batch/ont-10` (#4502); I'll retarget it to `main` once #4502 merges, per the cop's call. rc.1 is tagged after this merges.

**Problem.** binary-release.yml attached `apr` and `pv` only. 27 of the 29 workspace `[[bin]]`s never reached a tag. `asset_version_check.sh` also refused every line except `apr X.Y.Z (<sha>)`, so 28 of 29 real rc.1 lines failed.

**Change**
- New `build-all-bins` lane: x86_64 on yoga, aarch64 on gx10, gnu target, built in `rust:1.93.0-bullseye`.
  - The bin set and the cargo selection come from `scripts/nightly_manifest.py bins` run on the tag tree, exactly as nightly.yml does it. There is no second list.
  - `apr` and `pv` stay on their dedicated lanes. A second `pv-<tag>-<target>` from this lane would clobber the pv asset.
  - Before upload, each bin must pass `asset_version_check.sh TAG SHA LINE <bin>`, `--help`, the GLIBC_2.31 floor, and `nightly_manifest.py smoke`.
  - After upload, every asset is read back from the release.
  - Assets are named `<bin>-<tag>-<target>.tar.gz` + `.sha256`, so `promote_rc.sh` renames them like the other assets.
- `asset_version_check.sh`:
  - Takes an optional BIN argument, defaulting to apr, so 3-arg callers are unchanged. The name is compared as a literal prefix.
  - Accepts the ` (<description>)` that pv and pv-sat print after the sha.
  - 12 new case rows.
- `aprender-cgp` now prints its `[[bin]]` name; its clap name was `cgp`.

**Evidence**
- Ran the new check on all 29 `--version` lines of a stamped `v0.70.0-rc.1` build at 9f5609568: 29/29 ok.
- aprender-ptx-debug's deprecation notice goes to stderr, and the lane reads stdout only.
- `--self-test` PASS.
- Two mutants each turn the case table red: ignoring the bin name gives 6 FAIL rows, and a greedy sha field gives 1.
- `cargo test -p aprender-cgp --lib --test integration`: 121 + 29 passed.
- `cargo fmt` clean; actionlint shows only pre-existing info-level notes.

**Known gap.** `check_release_assets.sh`, the `assets` skip gate, still lists the 18 apr/pv assets. A release that has those 18 but is missing only all-bins assets would skip this lane. A follow-up can derive the list.

keep-open: #4520 is the LADDER-HOST-SAFE epic; this PR removes one host-memory hazard (whole-file GGUF reads on header-only verbs) and does not complete the epic.

Header-only verbs: `apr inspect` on GGUF parses only the header prefix instead of reading the whole file.

- `GgufReader::header_from_file` uses a growing prefix: the first read is 16 MiB and it grows to a 256 MiB cap. A header past the cap is **refused rather than read whole** (quorum round 1 finding). `header_from_file_within(path, first, cap)` is exposed so tests can pin the cap.
- Measured on a real 27B GGUF (`apr inspect --json`): bytes read went from 16.7 GB to 16 MB, peak RSS from 32.8 GB to 75 MB, and wall time from 62 s to 0.24 s. The JSON output is identical.
- New tests:
  - `a_header_longer_than_the_first_prefix_still_parses` (700k-token vocab fixture)
  - `a_header_past_the_cap_is_refused_not_read_whole`. Mutating the cap to `usize::MAX/2` makes it fail.
- Tests: aprender-core `format::gguf`/`prefix`/`rosetta` 661 pass, and apr-cli `inspect` 141 pass.

Closes #4351

`pv`'s proof_status Lean scan used a plain substring match for `sorry`. It refused credit to sorry-free theorems when a doc comment or string said "sorry", or when the theorem was cited in the `Theorems.<Domain>.<File>` form.

**What changes** (`crates/aprender-contracts/src/proof_status.rs`)
- `lean_has_sorry` reads Lean tokens:
  - skips line comments, nested block comments, strings and char literals;
  - treats identifiers such as `sorry_free` as names, not the `sorry` term;
  - fails closed: an unterminated comment or string counts as sorry.
- The `Theorems.<Domain>.<File>` citation now resolves to its file.
- Quorum fix: a char literal like `'"'` no longer opens a phantom string that hid a real `sorry`.

The two fix commits come from `origin/GH-4351-lean-scan-false-negatives`, cherry-picked onto main unchanged.
